items.prose:
```text
$ g++ -std=c++17 -Wall pnl.cpp -o pnl
pnl.cpp:7:12: warning: unused variable 'fees' [-Wunused-variable]
```
items.question: What is true now?

options.text: `./pnl` exists and runs; `fees` is worth a look
There is no executable until the warning is fixed
options.why: You read `warning` as `error`. Only errors stop the build.

options.text: `./pnl` runs the version from before this build
options.why: With no errors, the linker wrote a fresh `pnl`.

options.text: You must run g++ again without `-Wall`
options.why: `-Wall` only adds warnings. It never stops a build.

feedback.correct: A warning is advice; the build finished.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Does a warning stop a build?

explain.text: Only an `error:` stops the build, so `pnl` was written. The warning says `fees` is declared and never used, which can mean a forgotten step in a P&L.

byKey.true: The `double` on the left does not reach the right side. `qty / lots` divides two `int`s and gives 0.

items.question: What is `turns` at the end?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write out each value of `i`.

byKey.seven: You counted 3 to 9 one at a time. The step is `i += 2`.
byKey.five: 11 fails the test `i < 10`, so there is no fifth turn.

items.question: Which messages come from the linker rather than the compiler? Select all that apply.

options.why: A missing `;` is found while reading one file: that is the compiler.

options.text: `'annualise' was not declared in this scope`
options.why: An unknown name in one file is a compiler error. The linker only matches names across object files.

feedback.correct: The linker reports missing or doubled bodies across files.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which problems need more than one file to see?

explain.text: The compiler reads one `.cpp` at a time, so it reports syntax and unknown names. The linker joins the object files, so it reports a body that is missing or defined twice.

items.question: What does `volume` hold, in practice?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. An `int` wraps after 2,147,483,647.

byKey.true: That is the true total, but an `int` cannot hold it. It wraps by 2³², 4,294,967,296.
byKey.max: An `int` does not stop at its limit. It wraps round to negative values.
byKey.sign: 3,000,000,000 − 4,294,967,296 is below zero: the counter wraps past the largest int into negative numbers. A positive 1,294,967,296 drops that minus sign.

explain.text: The true sum, 3,000,000,000, is 2³² too big for the wrapped result: 3,000,000,000 − 4,294,967,296 = −1,294,967,296. A volume counter must be a `long long`.

items.prose: A risk check counts the days whose P&L lost more than the limit: a P&L below `-limit`. A loss of exactly the limit is not a breach.
items.question: Write `count_breaches(pnl, limit)`.

widget.how: The first Check downloads the C++ compiler (about 26 MB) and compiles in 10 to 15 s. Later Checks take 1 to 3 s. Check runs 5 hidden tests that call count_breaches; each must return exactly the expected count.

feedback.correct: Strictly below `-limit`, counted in one pass.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read the first failing test.

byKey.test-3: A loss of exactly 50 against a limit of 50 is not a breach. Use `<`, not `<=`.
byKey.test-1: Losses of 120.5 and 200 breach a limit of 100. Compare each P&L with `-limit`, not `limit`.

explain.text: A range-based `for` visits each day's P&L, and `x < -limit` counts only losses beyond the limit. An empty vector never enters the loop, so the count stays 0.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. C++ drops the fraction towards zero.

byKey.floor: You floored, as Python's `//` does. C++ truncates towards zero, so −2.25 becomes −2.
byKey.exact: Both operands are `int`, so the result is a whole number.
byKey.sign: −9 / 4 is −2.25, and truncating towards zero gives −2. A positive 2 drops the minus sign of the quotient.

explain.text: `-9 / 4` is −2.25 exactly, and C++ integer division drops the fraction towards zero: −2. Python's `-9 // 4` floors to −3.
